findings.title: Null max_segment_id check uses wrong semantics
findings.body: `_make_recording_filenames` returns [] when `row["max_segment_id"]` is None, but previously the test fixture used `max_segment_id: 0` to represent 'no segments'. Now a replay with a single segment (max_segment_id=0) would also be misinterpreted: `range(0+1)` still correctly includes segment 0, so that case is fine, but the change silently assumes None means no ingested segments without validating this assumption against production data where segment_id could legitimately be absent from Snuba aggregation (e.g. due to Function('max', ...) returning NULL for an empty group), potentially masking real deletions of orphaned recordings when the aggregation subtly differs from expectations. This should be verified against the exact Snuba NULL-max behavior to ensure deletions aren't silently skipped for replays with ingested but unlinked segment metadata.

findings.title: get_environment_info swallows all exceptions broadly
findings.body: The newly added `get_environment_info` catches a bare `Exception` and logs at `info` level, which could hide real bugs (e.g. AttributeError due to API misuse) as benign 'no environment' cases, making future regressions harder to detect in PR comment generation.

findings.title: Default behavior change for autofix automation tuning
findings.body: Changing `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` from "low" to "off" silently changes default behavior for all projects/orgs relying on this default, without an accompanying migration or changelog note found in the diff. This could unexpectedly disable autofix automation for existing users who had not explicitly set the option, since `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` project option default was also changed to "off" in projectoptions/defaults.py.

findings.title: Removed grouping option without migration/cleanup for existing stored values
findings.body: The option `grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent` was removed from registration, but if this option was previously set to a nonzero value in production (via admin), removing the registration could cause runtime errors or unexpected fallback behavior when the system tries to read an option that's no longer registered. No cleanup/migration is shown for existing stored option values.

findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty data behind new feature flag
findings.body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` with completely empty hardcoded data instead of the actual `result`/`eventView` data used by `StyledSimpleTableChart`. This means any organization with this feature flag enabled will see an always-empty table widget in dashboards, a significant regression that silently discards real data.

findings.title: updateLocationWithAggregateFields silently drops non-BaseVisualize/Visualize items
findings.body: The function assumes every non-BaseVisualize aggregateField is a plain GroupBy JSON-serializable object, but if a `Visualize` instance (not BaseVisualize) is passed directly (as hinted by other code paths using `Visualize` class instances interchangeably with BaseVisualize), `JSON.stringify(aggregateField)` on a class instance may not serialize as expected (methods are dropped, but internal fields like `selectedChartType` could leak unexpectedly into the URL), given the Visualize class has private fields and getters not meant for direct JSON serialization in this flattened path.

findings.title: Analytics event name changed without checking consistency with existing event key definitions
findings.body: The event name was changed from `replay.view_html` to `replay.view-html`, matching the type definition in `replayAnalyticsEvents.tsx`. This appears intentional and consistent, but renaming the actual Amplitude/analytics event key for an existing feature breaks continuity of previously collected analytics data under the old event key, which could affect historical reporting/dashboards unless this was already broken (i.e., events never actually fired due to the mismatch) prior to this fix. No dashboard migration or backward compatibility handling is mentioned.
